name: Amcor plc
executive_summary: Amcor is a global flexible and rigid packaging leader that completed its transformational Berry Global merger on 30 April 2025, roughly doubling scale to ~$23.5bn revenue and ~75,000 employees. The quantitative screen rates AMCR a **buy** on cheapness, dividend yield (~5.7%), and FCF yield (~7.1%), but fails most quality and deep-value models owing to elevated leverage, modest ROE (9.4%), and post-merger accounting noise. FY2026 GAAP net income rose sharply to $1.1bn (adjusted net income $1.9bn) as Berry synergies materialise, yet reported operating margin compressed to ~8.1% and organic volumes remain soft. The central debate is whether Berry integration, portfolio simplification, and deleveraging will convert a leveraged income compounder into a durable quality holding — or leave shareholders exposed to integration risk, goodwill impairment, and cyclical/resin-pass-through headwinds.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, AMCR offers a **cash-return-oriented entry** into a quasi-oligopoly packaging franchise at a screen composite score of 78% (6/22 models passed; families: cheapness, dividend, risk). The business generates substantial operating cash — **$2.15bn in FY2026** per the 10-K — and management has maintained a rising dividend through the merger, lifting the quarterly cash dividend to **$0.65 per share** (post 1-for-5 reverse split, January 2026) while declaring investment-grade access to debt markets.

The Berry combination is the value catalyst: management reports synergy delivery ahead of plan (news coverage cites ~$285m realised synergies and 32% EBITDA growth in Q4 FY26), and adjusted EBIT reached **$2.81bn** in FY2026 versus **$1.72bn** in FY2025 (10-K reconciliation). Scale should improve procurement, footprint utilisation, and customer cross-sell across nutrition, health, beauty and wellness end-markets that are structurally less cyclical than industrial packaging.

However, this is **not** a classic Graham or Buffett quality pass: debt/equity of ~128%, Piotroski F-Score 5/9, ROE below 12%, and EV/EBIT ~27x (screen failure on Acquirer's Multiple) all flag that the market is pricing integration success, not distress. The buy case rests on **FCF yield (~7.1% screen TTM) exceeding earnings yield (~5.2%)**, dividend growth continuity, and a credible path from **net debt of $12.9bn** (June 2026) toward sub-3.5x leverage as Berry cash flows accrue — not on pristine balance-sheet quality.
financial_review:
**Annual trend (10-K filings, FY ends 30 June)**

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | $13,640m | $15,009m | $23,506m |
| Operating income | $1,214m | $1,009m | $1,899m |
| Net income (Amcor plc) | $730m | $511m | $1,106m |
| Adjusted EBIT | $1,560m | $1,723m | $2,813m |
| Adjusted net income | $1,015m | $1,136m | $1,863m |
| Operating cash flow | $1,321m | $1,390m | $2,151m |
| CapEx | $492m | $580m | $922m |
| Net debt (year-end) | $6,111m | $13,271m | $12,897m |
| Total debt | $6,699m | $14,098m | $14,012m |
| Cash | $588m | $827m | $1,115m |

*Source: FY2024 10-K (Aug 2024), FY2025 10-K (Aug 2025), FY2026 10-K (Aug 2026) consolidated statements.*

**Interpretation:** Pre-merger Amcor was a stable ~$13–15bn revenue generator with mid-single-digit operating margins. FY2025 GAAP earnings fell (net income $511m) on **$307m** of restructuring/transaction/integration expense and Berry purchase-accounting charges (inventory amortisation $133m, transaction costs $169m). FY2026 reflects a full year of Berry: revenue +57%, adjusted EBIT +63%, and OCF +55%, while net debt edged down ~$374m from the post-merger peak.

Implied FY2026 free cash flow (OCF less PP&E/intangible capex per cash-flow statement) is approximately **$1.23bn** ($2,151m − $922m), versus dividend cash outflow of **$1,195m** — tight gross coverage, though integration-related working-capital swings and divestiture proceeds ($272m proceeds from divestitures in FY2026) affect the run-rate. The screen's TTM FCF of **$1.50bn** may reflect a different TTM window; filing-based FY2026 FCF is lower.

**Balance sheet (June 2026, 10-K):** Total assets $37.1bn; goodwill **$12.1bn**; other intangibles $6.6bn; shareholders' equity $11.8bn. Tangible book is deeply negative post-merger — typical for serial acquirers but relevant for asset-based screens (Graham Net-Net failed; NCAV unavailable).

**Interim releases (10-Q)**

- **Q1 FY2026** (Sep 2025): First full post-merger quarter; filings confirm merger-driven scale-up and elevated integration costs (body extract available).
- **H1 FY2026** (Dec 2025): Net sales **$11,194m** vs $6,594m prior year (+70%); operating income **$792m** (margin 7.1% vs 9.2%); net income **$439m**; diluted EPS **$0.95** (10-Q, Feb 2026).
- **9M FY2026** (Mar 2026): Net sales **$17,108m** vs $9,927m (+72%); operating income **$1,253m** (margin **7.3%** vs 9.3%); net income **$717m**; adjusted EBIT **$1,977m** vs $1,112m (+78%). Ex-merger organic net sales declined ~**2%** (volumes −3%, price/mix +1%). Net debt at 31 March 2026: **$14.3bn** (10-Q, May 2026).
- **Segment 9M FY2026:** Flexible packaging adjusted EBIT margin stable at **13.5%**; rigid packaging at **10.6%** (up from 7.6%) but legacy rigid volumes weak ex-merger.

**Other filing events:** 8-K (Nov 2025) documents **€1.5bn** senior note issuance to refinance Berry secured debt and commercial paper. No going-concern language in available extracts; management states covenant compliance (leverage ≤3.9x, stepping to 4.25x post-acquisition) as of June 2026.

**Gaps:** Yahoo `financials_annual.json` stops at FY2025 and was **not** used for FY2026 figures. Eight 8-K filings in the index lack body extracts. No separate trading-update regime filings. FY2026 is the first full Berry year — year-on-year comparisons are merger-distorted throughout.
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and integration:** Net debt ~$12.9bn; interest expense **$676m** in FY2026 (vs $396m FY2025). Bank facilities require leverage ≤3.9x (4.25x temporarily post-deal). Early redemption of ~$2.9bn Berry secured notes in FY2026 improves the maturity profile but refinancing risk remains in a 4.7% 10-year rate environment (macro marker only). PwC flagged **goodwill impairment testing for Global Rigid Packaging** ($6.1bn goodwill) as a critical audit matter in the FY2026 10-K.

**Operational/cyclical:** Organic volumes down ~2–3% in 9M FY2026. Resin and raw-material pass-through lag could compress margins — filings estimate a 1% unrecovered resin cost increase would hit PBT by ~$85m (FY2026 sensitivity). Highly inflationary Argentina accounting added $19–53m losses in prior years; still ~1% of sales.

**Regulatory/strategic:** August 2025 portfolio review identified **$2.5bn of sales** for potential divestiture/restructuring (10-Q risk factor); execution uncertainty and business disruption risk. Sustainability and plastic-packaging regulation remain structural overhangs for the sector (not quantified in extracts).

**Governance/accounting:** 1-for-5 reverse split (Jan 2026) and fiscal-year change to calendar year-end (transition report due) add comparability complexity. Berry internal controls excluded from FY2025 ICOFR assessment; integration ongoing. Berry customer-relationship intangible valuation ($5.5bn) was a critical audit matter at acquisition.

**Pension:** Net periodic pension cost $31m FY2026; employee benefit obligations $309m (10-K balance sheet). Pension settlements of $26m in adjusted reconciliations.

**Liquidity:** Dividends ($1.2bn) nearly match filing-derived FCF; reliance on commercial paper ($1.29bn drawn) backstopped by $2.46bn undrawn revolver capacity.

**No going-concern flag** in available filing bodies; liquidity narrative is confident but dividend coverage on a pure FCF basis is thin.

RiskTags: leverage, competitive, cyclical, regulatory, pension, accounting, other
news_highlights:
News coverage in the manifest is **concentrated and thin** for a full year — essentially all ten articles date from **12–14 August 2026** around FY2026 results; no earlier headlines captured.

Material items:

- **"Amcor Q4 adjusted profit soars 40% on Berry integration"** (Yahoo Finance, 13 Aug 2026) — FY adj. net income $1.8bn (+64% y/y cited in summary).
- **"Amcor Stock Yields 5.5% With Earnings Growth Picking Up"** (Barron's via Yahoo, 12 Aug 2026) — Berry synergies supporting dividend narrative.
- **"Amcor (AMCR) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript"** (13 Aug 2026) — 32% EBITDA growth, $285m synergies referenced.
- **"The Bull Case For Amcor (AMCR) Could Change Following Higher Dividend After Q4 FY26 Earnings"** (13 Aug 2026) — Q4 sales $6,398m, net income $389m, dividend raised post reverse split.
- **"Amcor and Ocean Potion partner on sunscreen packaging"** (14 Aug 2026) — minor innovation/M&A colour only.

Earlier strategic context (from filings, not news): Berry merger closed 30 April 2025; €1.5bn and $1.5bn bond issuances Nov 2025–Mar 2026 for refinancing; portfolio review announced Aug 2025. **Flag: news archive is insufficient for a full-year event audit** — verify management changes, regulatory actions, and M&A outside this window independently.
research_rationale: Filings confirm improving adjusted earnings, synergy delivery, and modest deleveraging that support the screen's cash-yield buy signal, but compressed GAAP margins, heavy goodwill, tight FCF/dividend coverage, and integration/portfolio-review overhangs prevent full conviction on business quality.
